opex.text: The Company uses its liquidity to fund existing and future loan commitments, to fund maturing certificates of deposit and demand deposit withdrawals, to invest in other interest-earning assets and to meet operating expenses. At September 30, 2026, certificates of deposit maturing within the next 12 months totaled $729.4 million. Based upon historical experience, the Company anticipates that a significant portion of the maturing certificates of deposit will be redeposited with us.

prov.heading: Allowance for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The ACL which equals the sum of the ALL and the ACL on unfunded lending commitments, is established through provisions for credit losses. Management recalculates the ACL at least quarterly to reassess the estimate of credit losses for the total portfolio at the relevant reporting date. Under ASC Topic 326, the ACL is measured on a pool basis when similar risk characteristics exist. For each pool of loans, management also evaluates and applies qualitative adjustments to the calculated ACL based on several factors, including, but not limited to, changes in current and expected future economic conditions, changes in industry experience and industry loan concentrations, changes in the volume and severity of NPAs, changes in lending policies and personnel and changes in the competitive and regulatory environment of the banking industry. Loans that do not share similar risk characteristics are individually evaluated and are excluded from the pooled loan analysis.

The ACL policy described above is supplemented by periodic reviews and validations performed by independent loan reviewers. The results of the reviews are reported to the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors. The establishment of the ACL is significantly affected by management judgment. There is likelihood that different amounts would be reported under different conditions or assumptions.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
Noninterest expense for the third quarter of 2026 totaled $26.3 million, up $3.8 million, or 16.8%, from the third quarter of 2025. Noninterest expense increased over the comparable quarter primarily due to an increase in foreclosed assets, net (up $1.7 million primarily for write downs on foreclosed assets due to updated values or contracts), compensation and benefits (up $1.6 million), other expenses (up $356,000), and data processing and communication (up $278,000), which were partially offset by a decrease in occupancy (down $81,000).

Noninterest expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $73.8 million, up $7.3 million, or 11.0%, from the same period in 2025. Noninterest expense increased over the comparable quarter primarily due to an increase in compensation and benefits (up $4.4 million), foreclosed assets, net (up $1.5 million primarily for write downs on foreclosed assets due to updated values or contracts), the absence of a reversal to the ACL on unfunded commitments ($970,000), and other expenses (up $697,000), partially offset by a decrease in franchise and shares tax (down $222,000).

nonop.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonop.text:
Noninterest expense for the third quarter of 2026 totaled $26.3 million, up $3.8 million, or 16.8%, from the third quarter of 2025. Noninterest expense increased over the comparable quarter primarily due to an increase in foreclosed assets, net (up $1.7 million primarily for write downs on foreclosed assets due to updated values or contracts), compensation and benefits (up $1.6 million), other expenses (up $356,000), and data processing and communication (up $278,000), which were partially offset by a decrease in occupancy (down $81,000).

Noninterest expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $73.8 million, up $7.3 million, or 11.0%, from the same period in 2025. Noninterest expense increased over the comparable quarter primarily due to an increase in compensation and benefits (up $4.4 million), foreclosed assets, net (up $1.5 million primarily for write downs on foreclosed assets due to updated values or contracts), the absence of a reversal to the ACL on unfunded commitments ($970,000), and other expenses (up $697,000), partially offset by a decrease in franchise and shares tax (down $222,000).

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: Income tax expense for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $2.7 million and $8.5 million, respectively, compared to $3.2 million and $8.8 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. The Company's effective tax rates for the third quarters of 2026 and 2025 were 21.0% and 20.5%, respectively. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, the Company's effective tax rates were 20.4% and 20.3%, respectively.

net.text: The Company reported net income for the third quarter of 2026 of $10.1 million, or $1.28 diluted EPS, down $2.3 million, or 18.3%, compared to the third quarter of 2025. Net income for the third quarter of 2025 totaled $12.4 million, or $1.59 diluted EPS. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported net income of $33.1 million, or $4.21 diluted EPS, down $1.6 million from $34.7 million, or $4.41 diluted EPS, reported for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
Net interest income is the difference between the interest income earned on interest-earning assets, such as loans and investment securities, and the interest expense paid on interest-bearing liabilities, such as deposits and borrowings. The Company’s net interest income is largely determined by our net interest spread, which is the difference between the average yield earned on interest-earning assets and the average rate paid on interest-bearing liabilities, and the relative amounts of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities. The Company’s taxable equivalent ("TE") net interest spread was 3.40% and 3.26% for the quarters ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, and 3.43% and 3.19% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Net interest income totaled $35.9 million for the third quarter of 2026, up $1.8 million, or 5.3%, compared to the third quarter of 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net interest income totaled $106.2 million, up $7.0 million, or 7.1%, compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

The Company’s TE net interest margin, which is net interest income as a percentage of average interest-earning assets, was 4.19% and 4.10% for the quarters ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. For the same periods, the average loan yield was 6.40% and 6.53%, respectively.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
Noninterest income for the third quarter of 2026 totaled $4.2 million, up $463,000, or 12.4%, from $3.7 million earned for the same period in 2025. Noninterest income increased over the comparable period primarily due to increases in other income (up $215,000), bank card fees (up $127,000), and service fees and charges (up $104,000).

Noninterest income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $11.9 million, up $395,000, or 3.4%, from $11.5 million earned for the same period in 2025. Noninterest income increased over the comparable periods primarily due to increases in service fees and charges (up $294,000) and bank card fees (up $111,000).

intro.text: General. Home Bancorp, Inc. (the “Company”) is a Louisiana corporation and the holding company for Home Bank, N.A. (the “Bank”). The Bank, which is headquartered in Lafayette, Louisiana and is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, currently conducts business through 43 banking offices in the Acadiana, Baton Rouge, Greater New Orleans and Northshore (of Lake Pontchartrain) regions of south Louisiana, the Natchez region of west Mississippi and the Houston region of Texas. The Company is subject to regulation as a bank holding company by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (the “FRB” or the “Federal Reserve”). The Bank established HB Investment Fund I, LLC and HB Investment Fund II, LLC, wholly-owned subsidiaries of the Bank to invest in New Markets Tax Credits (“NMTC”) and Federal Tax Credits ("FTC") in our market areas.
